newsitem.title: MEXICO: UNESCO designates five sites in World Heritage.
newsitem.headline: UNESCO designates five sites in World Heritage.

text.p: A barrier reef in Belize, the Kamchatka volcanoes and Lake Baikal in Russia, Niger's "W" National Park and the Okapi wildlife reserve in Zaire have been added to UNESCO's World Heritage list, the U.N. body said on Thursday.

The list designates areas of natural beauty that deserve special protection. In addition, four other previously designated World Heritage sites were identified as being "in danger," the World Heritage Committee of UNESCO, which is meeting in the Mexican city of Merida on the Yucatan Peninsula, announced in a news release.
A total of 107 such sites have now been designated worldwide, the committee of the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation said.
Sites labeled in danger were the Simen National Park in Ethiopia, the Ichkeul National Park in Tunisia, the Garamba National Park in Zaire and the Rio Platano Biosphere in Honduras.
The barrier reef of Belize is considered the largest coral reef in the northern hemisphere and is home to exotic wildlife such as sea turtles, manatees and ocean crocodiles.
The Kamchatka peninsula has a large number of active volcanoes and an array of wildlife, while Baikal Lake in southeast Siberia contains 20 percent of the non-frozen fresh water in the world.

The "W" National Park in Niger, a humid region between forests and savannahs, is considered "indispensable" for the protection of diverse species. The Okapi Wildlife Reserve in Zaire is home to species of primates and birds that are in danger of extinction.

Of the sites in danger, the Simen park in Ethiopia is losing its Walia ibex and other mammals; the Ichkeul park in Tunisia has been endangered by the nearby construction of dams; the Garamba park in Zaire has seen its white rhinoceros population decline; and the Rio Platano Biosphere in Honduras is "severely threatened" by an expanding agricultural frontier and human population.
